subject: Follow-up: Greenwave discovery — data handling & access controls
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenwavehealth.com>, Marta Lopez <m.lopez@greenwavehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Greenwave discovery — data handling & access controls

Hi Aisha / Marta —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Call summary (30m):
- Primary scope: how Redwood would host and serve model inference for Greenwave patient-facing features (PHI/PII considerations).
- PII types discussed: patient identifiers, limited PHI fields (treatment codes, timestamps), and hashed patient IDs used for model inputs.
- Data residency: control plane in the US; Greenwave requires that all inference inputs & logs remain in US-only regions.
- Retention & logging: Greenwave indicated a preference for 7-year retention on audit logs for billing & regulatory audits; shorter retention for transient inputs unless retained for investigations.
- Access controls: requirement for strict RBAC, least-privileged support access, and an auditable "emergency access" (break-glass) workflow that records approver, justification, and token scope.

Requested items we agreed to provide:
1) Redwood security summary (SOC2 highlights + RBAC support + support access playbook) — I attached an initial one.
2) A sample mutual action plan / MVP rollout schedule for controls and residency testing.
3) Answers to two clarifications you raised: a) what data is logged by default (request metadata vs. full inputs), and b) how break-glass events are captured and reviewed.

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll share the Redwood_Security_Summary_2025.pdf and a draft MVP mutual action plan by EOD tomorrow.
- Naomi / Rishi: can you prepare a one-page "RBAC + emergency access" tech note for the Greenwave InfoSec team? Aim for items we can commit to in a POC (e.g., strict role scopes, support session justification, 7-day vs. 7-year retention options).
- Aisha: please share the Greenwave compliance contact and any checklist file you want us to review.

Thanks — keen to keep momentum and turn this into a short pilot we can scope next week.

Best,
Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Summary_2025.pdf; MVP_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Greenwave discovery — data handling & access controls

Diego — thanks for the tidy recap. A few internal notes and an outline we can reuse for the response to Greenwave: 

Internal quick plan:
- Ownership: Rishi (security/architecture) will lead the RBAC & logging spec; Tessa will handle product/ops questions (retention windows, quotas, batching).
- RBAC approach: provide role templates (Admin, Support-ReadOnly, Support-Scoped, Auditor). For Support-Scoped we should demonstrate scoping by project and by token lifetime (e.g., 4-hour limited token).
- Emergency access (break-glass): implement as time-limited elevation tied to an approval ticket; all actions should be recorded in immutable audit logs and surface to Greenwave in a daily digest + retain for the requested retention period.
- Logging/retention: default request metadata logged for 90 days; provide options: 90 days (default), 1 year, 7 years (compliance tier with additional controls). Need to confirm costs / implications with billing.

Action items for this thread: 
1) Rishi: draft a one-page RBAC + emergency-access tech note by EOD tomorrow.
2) Tessa: short note on retention options and how we map retention tiers to policy configs.
3) Diego: send the security summary and ask for Greenwave's compliance checklist.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Greenwave discovery — data handling & access controls

Hi Diego / Naomi —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from Greenwave InfoSec and next asks: 

Clarifications / requirements:
1) Data residency: confirmed — all inference inputs, outputs, and audit logs must be stored and processed solely in US regions. We need contractual language that excludes any cross-border replication by default (exceptions require written approval).
2) Retention: our baseline requirement for audit logs is 7 years, but we can negotiate shorter retention for full request payloads. We prefer that raw inputs be configurable and not retained by default unless flagged for incident investigation.
3) Emergency access: must require two approvers (one from InfoSec and one from Ops) for any elevation. Each event must include: approver names, justification, start/end timestamps, and linked ticket ID. Events must be immutable and exportable for audits.
4) Support access: Greenwave requires time-bound, least-privilege sessions. Support engineers should only be able to view derived outputs and metadata unless higher-level access is approved by InfoSec.

Attached is our internal checklist: GW_compliance_checklist.xlsx. Our security team would like the RBAC tech note and an example emergency-access audit entry. Please include a proposed SLA on response time for break-glass requests (we expect 1 hour for emergency ack).

Security contact: security@greenwavehealth.com

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Senior PM, Greenwave Health
aisha.patel@greenwavehealth.com

Aisha — thanks, and appreciated the checklist. Next steps and what we'll deliver this week: 

Committed deliverables by Fri, 23 Jan: 
- One-page RBAC + emergency-access tech note (Rishi) — includes role templates, approval flow, and a sample immutable audit entry.
- Retention options and cost implications (Tessa) — maps 90d / 1yr / 7yr tiers to config flags and estimated incremental cost.
- Contract language draft for US-only residency and break-glass approvals (legal intake) — I'll loop in legal after we finalize the tech notes.
- Redwood_Security_Summary_2025.pdf (attached) — short overview of SOC2 controls, encryption, and KMS options.

Proposed pilot: 4-week POC on a scoped dataset with US-only residency and time-limited support access. I'll attach a draft MVP_mutual_action_plan.xlsx for your review. Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up for Wed 28 Jan to finalize acceptance criteria? Please let me know times that work.

Deal id: RW-4821-GREEN — I'll record these deliverables in HubSpot and share progress links.
